subject: geography
title: KS3 Geography - Tectonic Hazards
subtitle: Revision pack covering earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunamis, plate boundaries and hazard management.
description: A KS3 revision pack on tectonic hazards, including the structure of the Earth, plate boundaries, earthquakes, volcanoes and tsunamis. It uses named examples and data-style questions to help students explain why impacts vary between places.

data.title: How an earthquake happens
data.instruction: Put the earthquake process in the correct order.
items: Plates move slowly along a fault or plate boundary.
Rough plate edges become stuck by friction.
Pressure builds up as the plates keep trying to move.
The rocks suddenly break or slip.
Energy travels out as seismic waves.
The ground shakes and an earthquake is felt.

data.title: How a destructive boundary forms a volcano
data.instruction: Put the volcano formation steps in the correct order.
items: An oceanic plate moves towards a continental plate.
The denser oceanic plate is subducted beneath the continental plate.
The sinking plate begins to melt in the mantle.
Magma rises because it is less dense than surrounding rock.
Magma breaks through the crust as lava and ash.
A volcano is built up over time.

data.title: How a tsunami forms
data.instruction: Put the tsunami formation steps in the correct order.
items: Two plates become stuck beneath the ocean.
A sudden slip lifts or drops part of the sea floor.
Water above the sea floor is displaced.
Waves travel quickly across deep ocean water.
The waves slow down in shallow coastal water.
Water piles up and floods low-lying coastlines.

data.title: Hazard management cycle
data.instruction: Put the hazard management cycle in the correct order.
items: Prepare with hazard maps, drills and supplies.
Respond with rescue, aid and emergency shelters.
Recover by repairing services and supporting survivors.
Mitigate by rebuilding stronger and improving plans.
Prepare again using lessons learned from the event.
